text:
maria (Support): heads-up — multiple hosted-api customers reporting 502/504 spikes for streaming and short-gen since ~09:45 PT. customers see timeouts then 502s from edge. attaching traces we have so far.

raj (Customer): 504 when doing streaming chat completions, happens after ~30s of token generation. curl sample: `curl -v -H 'Authorization: Bearer xxxxx' -d '{"model":"rwd-3b","input":"hello"}' https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate` 
trace id: trace-9a7b5c. also saw `upstream response timeout` in client logs.

maria (Support): repro steps from customer: 1) open streaming conn, 2) send prompt with long context (~2k tokens), 3) wait ~25-40s, 4) client sees stalled stream then 504. non-streaming short requests also get intermittent 502s.

carol (Eng-SRE): :eyes: can we get the edge logs + envoy/ingress metrics for the trace ids? suspect h2 stream windowing / connpool saturation. any recent auth cache changes?

maria (Support): pasted edge logs snippet: 
```
[2026-02-15T16:47:12Z] ingress: upstream request timed out after 30000ms, id=trace-9a7b5c, upstream=upstream-host-13
[2026-02-15T16:47:12Z] envoy: stream error: code=Internal, cause=upstream reset
```

maria (Support): customer also reports they rotated tokens yesterday. they use short-lived guest tokens, rotate every 15m.

dave (Eng-Platform): we rolled a small config tweak to h2 keepalive and pooled conn TTL at 08:30 PT — rolling back now to validate.

ingress-bot: deploy/rollback triggered by dave at 1725008400, change: h2_keepalive_idle=20s -> 10s, conn_pool_ttl=300s -> 120s.

carol (Eng-SRE): interesting — short conn_pool_ttl + token rotation can cause auth proxy churn. if upstreams drop idle streams quickly, long streaming will be re-routed to new conn and may lose KV cache. looking at per-route 5xx: spike aligned to 08:40-09:00 PT.

raj (Customer): we also saw increased latency to authz (auth-cache) ~50-200ms. maybe our token refresh pattern + edge churn exposing auth backend.

carol (Eng-SRE): action items: 1) rollback dave's keepalive/ttl change (in progress), 2) enable extra ingress debug for one shard and capture envoy admin /stats and upstream ejection logs, 3) ask eng-runtime to look at KV cache eviction when conn is reset.

maria (Support): engaged eng-runtime and eng-platform. assigning to @carol and @dave. sending customer a mitigation note: please try non-streaming short requests or reduce rotation briefly while we triage. :thumbsup:

dave (Eng-Platform): rollback started — will take ~6m to converge across regions. will DM when done.

carol (Eng-SRE): in parallel collecting pprof from edge-proxy shard-7 and envoy admin stats: `curl -s http://127.0.0.1:9901/stats | grep upstream_cx` and `envoy clusters | grep ejection`

maria (Support): posted copy to customer with trace id and timeline. customer responded: "we can keep rotation paused for 20m and test" — they are on standby.

ingress-bot: rollback completed at 1725010350 by dave, rollout-id=rb-20260215-01, status=converged.

carol (Eng-SRE): initial telemetry after rollback: 5xx rate down ~70% on affected routes, upstream ejection events decreasing. still seeing a few long-tail 502s correlated with auth-cache misses. next: add a short-term auth-cache grace window and a fix for conn rebind handling in runtime.

maria (Support): will update customer and close the escalation if they confirm stability in 30m. thanks all. :raised_hands:

raj (Customer): confirmed — after rollback no 504s in last 10m, will keep testing and report back. thanks for fast turnaround.
